chunks: He said, 'O my Lord, since You have led me into error, I will beguile them on earth and lead them astray, all of them.'

key_terms.لَأُغْوِيَنَّهُمْ: I will surely lead them astray

ai.seo_question: What did Adam say after being expelled from Paradise?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted as Satan’s boastful declaration of his mission to mislead humanity, stemming from his refusal to prostrate to Adam. It underscores the concept of *al-haqiqah al-ashadd* (the more severe reality) where divine permission for Satan’s trial serves as a mechanism for distinguishing the sincere from the heedless, a theme central to the doctrine of *al-Amr bayn al-Amrayn*. The verse highlights the cosmic struggle between divine wisdom and satanic corruption, framing earthly life as a testing ground where humans must actively resist temptation through faith and obedience.
